newsitem.title: Norwegian shares climb to new highs on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares climb to new highs on U.S. data.

text.p: Norwegian shares raced ahead and set a new all-time high for the third consecutive session on Friday after weaker than expected U.S. nonfarm payroll figures sent stock markets climbing.
Dealers said sentiment also was positive following recent good company results and the government's presentation of the 1997 budget proposal.
The Total index stormed ahead to a peak at 863.41 points before easing back at the close to end 0.87 percent up at 863.18 points.
Turnover was a bumper 1.52 billion crowns, of which 772 million crowns were accountable to the sale of a 1.8 million share block in insurance group Storebrand.
Tiger Management sold the block in line with a ruling from the Finance Ministry that it must reduce its shareholding to 10 percent before year end in accordance with Norwegian securities regulations.
Brokers said Tiger ploughed into options after the sale, which lifted Storebrand's share price. The stock gained almost five percent, or 1.70 crowns, to 36.70 crowns.
